Close-cropped neat — short all over, trimmed tight, clean lines at temples and nape.
Military fade — shaved to skin on sides, short dense crop left on top.
Side-parted short — combed flat to one side, kept with tallow or road-dust pressed smooth.
Slicked-back — medium length, combed straight back from forehead, stiff with dried sweat.
Tousled short crop — finger-length on top, unstyled, pushed forward by habit or wind.
Shoulder-length tied in a low queue — gathered neatly at the nape with a leather cord.
High topknot — long hair wound tight at the crown, secured with a knotted thong.
Warrior half-up — sides hang loose, upper section pulled back and pinned at the crown.
Long and loose — past shoulder blades, uncombed, parted wherever wind decides it.
Single thick braid down the back — woven tight at the crown, reaching mid-back.
Multiple small braids — dozens of thin plaits pulled back and bundled together at the neck.
Dreadlocks gathered back — thick locked ropes collected behind the head with a wide cloth band.
Undercut with a long top — sides cropped short, top left long and swept loosely aside.
Shaved sides with a center tail — strip of hair runs crown to nape, braided thin.
Wind-swept medium — jaw-length, no product, blown permanently to one side from riding.
Kept-short receding hairline — hair cropped close to work with what remains, neat and unfussy.
Bald by choice — head shaved to bare skin, maintained deliberately with a blade each week.
Fine straight elven length — falls ruler-straight to the waist, tucked behind the ears while traveling.
Wet-slicked from travel — medium hair plastered flat by rain or river crossing, not yet dried.
Chin-length pushed back — falls to the jaw, shoved behind ears to clear the face.
Cropped with a hard part — short sides, razor-lined part cut deep to one side, worn flat.
Rough bowl cut — blunt-trimmed all around at ear level, self-cut or camp-cut, uneven hem.
Short textured crop — thumb-length, dense, naturally lifted at the crown with no styling effort.
Pulled-forward fringe — medium length, all combed toward the forehead, fringe cut blunt across the brow.
Loose low knot — long hair twisted once and tucked under itself, knot sitting low on the skull.
Chin-length and pushed back — falls to the jaw, swept back off the face without ties.
Loose medium with a center part — falls to the neck, split evenly, tucked behind both ears.
Cropped silver — short and tight, natural grey left uncolored, well-maintained against the scalp.
Pulled-back widow's peak — prominent point at the forehead, rest drawn back into a short tail.
Rough-chopped bowl — blunt uneven cut ringing the head, self-trimmed with a belt knife.
Cropped tight with a widow's peak — naturally sharp hairline left unaltered, sides and back cut very close.
Loose short layers — uneven choppy cut, sits just above the ears, no styling, grows out between towns.
Bound travel knot — medium-length hair twisted into a rough coil at the back, secured with a stick.
Short on top, longer in back — front kept cropped, nape hair growing out to a short trailing fringe.
Loose waves to the shoulder — naturally wavy, cut without precision, worn open and mostly ignored while traveling.
Shaved to stubble — head hair grown just enough to show color and direction, kept by razor every few days.
Temple-shaved with a full long top — hair above the ears left full and long, sides stripped clean to skin.
